title: The US-Canada Border Is Thousands of Short Lines #shorts
summary: A true parallel curves, but since a 1925 treaty the 49th-parallel boundary is defined as straight lines between monuments; the line was drawn on paper first and traced on the ground later.
tags: why is the us canada border straight
sources: Treaty of 24 February 1925, Article II: the boundary along the 49th parallel shall be defined as consisting of a series of right or straight lines joining adjacent monuments, replacing the definition under which the line between monuments had the curvature of the parallel (Foreign Relations of the United States 1925, Office of the Historian): https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1925v01/d387

The 49th parallel boundary actually consists of several chords drawn between astronomically determined points on the curved parallel; Lake of the Woods to the Rockies agreed in the Convention of 1818, Rockies to the Strait of Georgia by the Oregon Treaty of 1846 (The Canadian Encyclopedia, Forty-ninth Parallel): https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/forty-ninth-parallel

The first instance of a boundary drawn first on paper then traced on the ground; latitude determined with the zenith telescope (Talcott method) (American Society of Civil Engineers, Historic Civil Engineering Landmark: United States-Canadian Boundary Survey): https://www.asce.org/about-civil-engineering/history-and-heritage/historic-landmarks/united-states-canadian-boundary-survey

Map data: Natural Earth (public domain) https://www.naturalearthdata.com and US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain) https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/carto-boundary-file.html

scenes.narration: A true line of latitude curves. This border doesn't. Since a {1925|nineteen twenty-five} treaty, it runs straight from monument to monument.
It was drawn on paper first, and traced on the ground later.
So up close, the border is thousands of short straight lines.
